input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 satisfies the preferred position in full: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on thirty days' written notice, Vendor must promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period (a pro-rata refund), and Vendor is expressly denied any corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term. No other termination provision (§§ 9.1–9.3, 9.5, 10.1–10.2, 27.3) grants Vendor a convenience right, and § 8.2 non-renewal is Customer-controlled with a Vendor reminder obligation, so it is a renewal mechanic rather than a Vendor mid-term convenience right. No early-termination fee or penalty appears anywhere. The only tension is § 2.1's take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights," which sits with the minimum-commitment rule rather than T4C and is not flagged twice here. No redline proposed.
